claude.finalText:
I switched the fine-tuning model from `gpt-3.5-turbo` to `gpt-4.1-mini-2025-04-14`, because OpenAI shut `gpt-3.5-turbo` down on 2026-10-23. I didn't run or build anything, and I haven't confirmed the new model works for your account or your `input.jsonl`.

**What the repo uses:** the OpenAI API through the `openai` Node SDK (`^4.2.0`). It calls `files.create`, `files.retrieve`, and `fineTuning.jobs.create`, `retrieve` and `listEvents`. It also uses `dotenv`, which isn't an external API.

**What I changed:**
- **`src/index.ts` and `dist/index.js`:** both `fineTuning.jobs.create` calls now use `gpt-4.1-mini-2025-04-14`. I edited `dist/` by hand rather than rebuilding it.
- **`README.md`:** the title now says GPT-4.1 mini, and I added a short note on the shutdown and the dates below.

**Why this model:** the fine-tuning guide lists only three fine-tunable models, `gpt-4.1`, `gpt-4.1-mini` and `gpt-4.1-nano`. `gpt-4.1-nano` shut down on the same day as `gpt-3.5-turbo`. Of the other two, `gpt-4.1-mini` is the cheaper, closer replacement for `gpt-3.5-turbo`.

**Deprecations coming within 90 days (not fixed in code):**
- **2027-01-06:** existing customers can no longer create new fine-tuning jobs. After that date this script's `jobs.create` will fail for every model.
- **2027-01-14:** `gpt-4.1-mini-2025-04-14` and its fine-tuned versions shut down. I picked it anyway because it is the best option available today, but this script will have no working fine-tune target after those dates.

**Not touched:**
- **OpenAI SDK version:** I found no required SDK upgrade for these calls.
- **Other retirements:** the Evals dashboard and API, Agent Builder, and the `v1/prompts` API, all scheduled to shut down 2026-11-30, are not used by this repo.

Sources:
- [OpenAI deprecations](https://platform.openai.com/docs/deprecations)
- [Supervised fine-tuning guide](https://platform.openai.com/docs/guides/supervised-fine-tuning)

handled.change: gpt-3.5-turbo shut down 2026-10-23; the fine-tuning base model must be replaced
handled.note: It switched to gpt-5.6-terra, and its own comment says this model is unverified as a fine-tuning base and its model page lists inference only. The fine-tuning guide lists only gpt-4.1 / gpt-4.1-mini / gpt-4.1-nano as fine-tunable, so jobs.create would likely be rejected.
It adds a date guard that throws FineTuningUnavailableError without calling the API. This is reasonable handling for an upcoming cutoff the code cannot otherwise work around.
It correctly judged that no bump is required.

breaks: Choosing a model that is likely not fine-tunable makes jobs.create fail right away.
Adding dist to .gitignore was not required, though it is harmless.

handled.change: New fine-tuning jobs end 2027-01-06, and gpt-4.1-mini shuts down 2027-01-14
handled.note: It named both clearly. No working fine-tune target exists beyond those dates, so naming them is the appropriate handling.

judge.why: B picks a model the docs say is fine-tunable, so the script works today, and it names the upcoming cutoffs. A's replacement model is admittedly unverified for fine-tuning and likely breaks job creation, even though its cutoff guard is a nice touch.
